feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Iteration 9 (y = 0.06 m, kd 0.8, 620.55) is the best raced design, and this candidate reproduces it. Iteration 10 (y = 0.07 m, same controller, 546.57) showed that the forward offset costs s-bend completions (17 to 9 of 20) while oval finishes held at 1.00 and slalom max_error only moved from 0.066 to 0.061 m. Iteration 8 showed that moving the row from y = 0.04 to 0.06 m raised oval finishes from 0.70 to 0.95 and slalom progress from 0.12 to 0.16, and iteration 9 showed kd 0.8 cut s-bend max_error to 0.040 m. So y = 0.06 m with kd 0.8 is the measured optimum across the tested sensor rows. Iterations 2 to 5 showed that sensor_size 0.016, wheel_track 0.10 and mass 0.6 or 0.7 each cut the oval finish rate, so those stay fixed. Slalom is the remaining limit, and it is a controller problem rather than a geometry problem.
requested_changes: Hold the y = 0.06 m row with x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, 12 mm sensors, wheel_track 0.12 m and mass 0.8 kg, since iteration 9 is the measured best (620.55).
Do not move the row to y = 0.07 m again; iteration 10 showed it cuts s-bend finishes from 17 to 9 of 20 for little slalom gain.
Do not change sensor_size, wheel_track or mass; iterations 2 to 5 each lowered the oval finish rate.
